subject: Geo-locking & retention commitments for Private deployment
messages:
From: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@acme-corp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Geo-locking & retention commitments for Private deployment

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our compliance team has a few follow-up questions specific to Private/VPC deployments (we're evaluating Redwood for a pilot that must remain strictly within EU jurisdictions). Can you confirm the following items so we can move this through procurement? Short bullets are fine.

1) Residency: Can you guarantee that Customer Data for a Private deployment will remain in EU region(s) only (no cross-region replication or failover outside EU) unless Acme expressly requests it?
2) Storage & Control: In a VPC/private install, is the storage fully customer-controlled (customer-managed buckets/volumes) or does Redwood retain any managed snapshot copies in other accounts/regions?
3) Encryption & Keys: Do you support BYOK (customer KMS/HSM) for all data at rest and snapshot encryption? Any limitations?
4) Deletion: If we request data deletion, what are the timelines for logical deletion, cache invalidation, and irreversible removal/crypto-erase of underlying storage? Can you provide evidence/certificates of deletion?
5) Backups & Snapshots: What is the default retention for backups/snapshots and can we opt to set retention to zero for covered datasets?
6) Logs & Audits: How long are audit logs retained by default and can we get exports for audit purposes?
7) Contractual language: Can Redwood accept binding residency/deletion commitments in an SOW or side letter?

If you have an existing compliance matrix or sample side-letter wording, that would speed things up on our side. We also may want to review your most recent SOC 2 summary.

Appreciate a consolidated response and any proposed next steps.

Best,
Amanda Lee
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_rfi.xlsx

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Geo-locking & retention commitments for Private deployment

Hi Amanda — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I'll loop in our security and product leads for exact timelines and proposed contract language, and I can attach our compliance matrix + SOC2 summary. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Quick bullets:
- Residency: For Private/VPC deployments we can pin storage to the region specified in the SOW (EU only). No automatic replication to non-EU regions unless explicitly requested.
- Storage: Customer-controlled storage model — volumes/snapshots live in the customer's cloud account or in a dedicated project chosen by the customer; Redwood does not retain independent copies outside that scope for normal operation.
- Encryption: We support BYOK (customer-managed KMS) for data at rest and snapshots. HSM integrations available for enterprise customers.
- Deletion: Logical deletion + cache invalidation typically initiated within 24 hours; underlying block storage crypto-erase / secure decommissioning target 30 days. We'll provide deletion audit entries.
- Backups: Default snapshot retention is 30 days; retention can be shortened or disabled by config for covered datasets as part of the deployment SOW.
- Logs: Audit logs retained 90 days by default; exports available to the customer.
- Contract: We can include residency and deletion commitments via SOW/side letter; we'll propose specific language.

I'll attach the compliance matrix and SOC2 summary and follow up with a draft side-letter example.

Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-private-compliance-matrix.xlsx

Folks — forwarding Acme's RFI (see below). They want clear, contractible commitments about EU-only storage and deletion evidence. Are the bullets below accurate enough to send back as a single consolidated response, or do we need to tighten timelines / change wording?

Proposed answers to include in external reply (draft):
- "Data residency: Customer Data for Private/VPC deployments will be stored only in the EU region(s) designated in the SOW. Redwood will not replicate Customer Data to regions outside the EU unless the Customer provides an explicit written request.
- Storage & control: Storage remains under Customer control (deployed into Customer-owned cloud project or dedicated customer project). Redwood will not make operational snapshots in other accounts/regions except for customer-authorized backups.
- Encryption & keys: Full support for BYOK. Snapshots are encrypted with the customer's keys.
- Deletion: Logical deletion and cache invalidation initiated within 24 hours of request. Redis/edge caches invalidated within 48 hours. Underlying volume crypto-erase/secure decommissioning completed within 30 days where possible; where physical media destruction language is used, replace with 'secure decommissioning/crypto-erase' for cloud environments.
- Backups: Default retention 30 days; Customer may request reduced retention or immediate deletion for specified datasets as part of SOW.
- Audit logs: Retention 90 days default; exports provided on request for audit.
- Contract: Redwood can agree to include residency and deletion commitments in a side letter or SOW; will provide sample wording and an attestation/cert of deletion upon completion.

Thoughts? If we can sign off I'll send this to Amanda + attach SOC2 and matrix.

-- Hannah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Geo-locking & retention commitments for Private deployment

Thanks for the draft, Hannah. A few suggested edits from security/product so we don't overpromise: 

- Residency: "Stored only in EU region(s) designated in the SOW" is fine. Clarify that in failover scenarios we will follow the runbook agreed in the SOW and notify customer; we should not commit cross-region failover without customer approval.
- Storage: Customer-controlled storage is correct for our Private deployment approach. Note: we may create short-lived operational snapshots for support in our managed tooling, but those are encrypted with customer keys and remain in the customer's tenant or a dedicated customer project. We should add an explicit line that operational debug snapshots are purged within 7 days unless preserved by customer request.
- Encryption: BYOK supported for volumes and snapshot keys; HSM/BYOK edge cases documented in the matrix.
- Deletion: Replace any mention of "physical media destruction" with "secure crypto-erase and logical sanitization." We should be explicit about the difference between: (a) logical deletion of application-level copies (24 hours), (b) cache invalidation (48 hours), and (c) secure decommissioning/crypto-erase of underlying volumes and snapshots (target 30 days). In some cloud providers, zeroing may take longer due to provider retention — call that out and add a clause that we'll provide deletion evidence (audit logs + exportable attestation).
- Backups: Default 30 days; allow Customer to set retention to 0 for specific datasets if required and agreed in the SOW.
- Logs: 90 days default; can extend with an add-on.

I'll approve this wording as long as we include the small operational caveats (short-lived debug snapshots, provider-level retention variance) and include a SOC2 summary attachment.

Karthik
Director, Security & Compliance

Hi Amanda — thanks for the patience. Below is a consolidated, contract-ready summary from our Security and Product teams. I've attached the compliance matrix and a SOC2 summary; I can also produce a draft side letter for signature.

Consolidated commitments (for Private/VPC deployments)
- Data residency: Customer Data will be stored only in the EU region(s) explicitly designated in the SOW. Redwood will not replicate Customer Data to non-EU regions unless the Customer provides explicit written authorization. In emergency failover scenarios, cross-region actions require prior agreement in the runbook in the SOW and Redwood will notify Customer as soon as practicable.
- Storage & control: Private deployments place storage into the Customer's cloud account or into a dedicated customer project controlled by the Customer. Operational snapshots created for support are encrypted with the Customer's keys and are retained only briefly (purged within 7 days unless Customer requests retention).
- Encryption & KMS: We support BYOK for all data-at-rest and snapshot encryption. HSM integrations are available for enterprise customers; details in the attached matrix.
- Deletion timelines & proof: Upon Customer request: (a) logical deletion of application-level copies and job queues initiated within 24 hours; (b) cache/edge invalidation completed within 48 hours; (c) secure decommissioning / crypto-erase of underlying volumes and snapshots targeted within 30 days. Note: actual physical media disposal language is replaced with "secure crypto-erase" for cloud environments; provider-imposed retention windows may occasionally extend timelines — we will document such cases. Redwood will provide deletion audit log entries and an exportable certificate of deletion on completion.
- Backups & snapshots: Default retention is 30 days; Customers may configure retention to a shorter window or request immediate deletion for specific datasets as part of the SOW.
- Audit logs: Default retention 90 days; log exports available on request. Extended retention is available as an add-on.
- Contractual commitments: Redwood can accept binding residency and deletion commitments via an SOW or side letter. We will provide sample SOW language and a side-letter draft for your legal/procurement review.

Next steps:
1) I'll send a draft side letter / SOW language (link attached) for your procurement team to review.
2) If Acme needs stronger retention guarantees or extended log retention, we can price those as part of the Dedicated/Private purchase order.
3) If you want a signed attestation after deletion, we will provide a deletion certificate and the supporting audit logs.
